svg.title: Landed Cost Stack Behind a $10 Supplier Price
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-landed-cost-stack; chapter number: 4; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Landed Cost Stack Behind a $10 Supplier Price; subtitle: Goods plus freight, duty and fees divided by units received; total range: $12,000 landed on 1,000 units, or $12 per unit versus a $10 supplier price; caption: Intel by CandiMentor's worked example shows the supplier invoice is only the starting point; freight, duty and fees add $2,000 across 1,000 units.; assumptions note: Low and high are equal because the example reports single figures. Trade Counsel separately stacks 3.4%, 7.5% and 12.5% into 23.4% duty on Chinese plastic bins.; note: Sources: Intel by CandiMentor [CvHvBnjwlJg @ 00:05:57], Trade Counsel [-WXoF_u08g0 @ 00:01:56], SKUio [DFZ8XDRkuCE @ 00:00:20].; buckets: label: Product; low: 10000; high: 10000; notes: Supplier invoice for 1,000 units; label: Freight; low: 1200; high: 1200; notes: Keep freight separate on the invoice and bill of lading; label: Duty; low: 500; high: 500; notes: Often arrives weeks later on the broker's bill (SKUio); label: Fees; low: 300; high: 300; notes: Broker and handling fees
